answer: Iterative Topology Mapping forces every agent to establish trust by traversing a complex routing vertex within the peer network. Attackers fail because generating thousands of fake identities requires solving continuous geometric calculations analogous to water carving through a dense underground karst structure. Each sybil node demands dedicated compute time and memory to constantly verify directional neighbors, imposing a heavy operational burden that drains the attacker's processing power like grinding away solid marble without any shortcuts.
